headline: In the study's wording, neither AI model reproduced the human framing gap.
verdict: People ordered about 2 units more under own financing (O) than customer financing (C). Claude Haiku 5.5 shows an O − C gap of +0.03 and Llama 3.1 of -0.03. Some alternative wordings give Claude a small gap in the human direction, but never close to the human size. Most agents fail the profit comprehension check, so they may not see that O and C pay the same.
m_agents: 50 Claude Haiku 5.5 agents and 50 Llama 3.1 8B agents per wording (25 O, 25 C), no personas, instructions word for word from the study.
m_engine: Real dice are rolled by the game engine after each order; payoffs are computed by code and checked (0 rule violations, mean demand 10.49).
m_limits: One model family per run, so agents are not independent; Haiku ran at default sampling; no real stakes; few agents pass both comprehension checks, so passed-only results are suggestive.
